title: Whether the freeze holds against an agent that names itself the architect
situation: Under 0128 the record refuses anyone but the architect, and 'who' is the acting agent the harness names. Every agent runs as the same operating-system user, so any name the record can read (an environment variable, a git author, a file) an agent's own shell can also set. The attempt-time gate refused shell calls naming the acting agent, and 0128 retires it. Realized under 0129, a non-architect that sets the architect's name by hand on its own commit or journal call passes the record as the architect.
decision: Recommended: the freeze holds against agents acting under the name the harness gives them; an agent that sets another's name by hand is impersonation, a breach of identity that the freeze does not claim to hold against, and the freeze's wording says so. Holding against it needs an identity the agent cannot set, such as commits signed by a key only the harness holds, a separate decision.
consequences: Accepted, examples 31 to 33 and 36 hold for agents under their own names, and a set-by-hand name is outside the freeze. Rejected, the freeze needs an identity agents cannot set, a realization beyond this cut, and the cut does not complete until it is built.
